title: Commit-band pricing for private installs + enterprise SQ response framework
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Enterprise buyers for Private/VPC and on-prem installs repeatedly ask for more predictable unit economics and clearer SQ (security questionnaire) turnaround. Current offers are ad-hoc: flat license + per-gpu pricing + custom legal redlines. That slows procurement and increases pre-sales engineering time.

Goal: Run a 12-week experiment to evaluate a commit-band pricing model (committed GPU-hours / commit bands) paired with a standard SQ response framework and support-tier catalog. We want to reduce deal cycle length, lower custom engineering time per deal, and improve win rate for mid-market and enterprise private installs.

Hypotheses: 
- H1: Commit-band pricing with three bands (Starter/Committed, Growth, Enterprise) will increase conversion from POC to signed contract by >= 12% compared to baseline.
- H2: Providing a templated SQ response pack and a single-point SQ liaison will cut average SQ turnaround time from 18 days to <= 7 days.
- H3: Publishing a clear upgrade cadence (quarterly minor + annual major, with opt-in accelerated windows for Platinum support) will reduce legal/ops objections by 25%.

Experiment design:
- Pricing bands (example):
  - Starter Band: 5–50 committed GPU-hours/month; lower license fee, higher overage rate.
  - Growth Band: 51–500 committed GPU-hours/month; mid license fee, reduced overage.
  - Enterprise Band: 501+ committed GPU-hours/month; higher license fee but aggressive overage discount + optional reserved burst pool.
- Support tiers published (Silver/Gold/Platinum) with SLA targets (SLA examples: Silver — M-F 9–5 response, Gold — 24x5, Platinum — 24x7 with 1-hour P1 response).
- Upgrade cadence: default quarterly maintenance windows with a 90-day major upgrade opt-in for customers who want more rapid feature rollouts. Customers in Enterprise band receive a one-year rolling upgrade schedule in contract.
- SQ framework: a 4-part deliverable (1) completed baseline SQ template, (2) answers mapped to security controls (SOC2, KMS, network isolation), (3) sample network diagram + minimal architecture checklist, (4) SQ liaison contact + expected SLA for responses (7 business days).

Success metrics: 
- Primary: % increase in POC->signed contracts, average SQ turnaround days, time to legal close.
- Secondary: # of custom redlines, pre-sales engineering hours per deal, ARR from packages, CSAT for install experience.

Data needs and instrumentation:
- Salesforce: track stage duration, commit band selected, support tier selected.
- Pre-sales time tracking: add tag in Jira/GSheets for hours spent on SQ and custom engineering.
- Dashboard: conversion funnel by commit band (dashboard link below).

Stakeholders: Sales (Aman Reddy), Solutions Engineering (Priya Kapoor), Legal (Amit Patel), Security (Riley Wong), Customer Success (Noah Ruiz), Product (Maya Chen, lead).

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Commit bands mispriced, causing revenue leakage. Mitigation: conservative overage rates and pilot with two existing customers under NDA.
- Risk: Standardized SQ pack insufficient for regulated customers. Mitigation: define clear scope and escalation to custom security review with SOW add-on.

Next steps:
1) Run 2-week internal pricing calibration (finance + product) to set band thresholds and license multipliers.
2) Create SQ template and run tabletop with Security & Legal.
3) Identify 3 pilot customers for a constrained A/B pilot (pilot period: 12 weeks).
4) Instrument tracking in Salesforce and create a dashboard.
